teaser: Have you ever wished to achieve two goals with a single effort? Let's explore how this idiom captures that concept.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Have you ever wished to achieve two goals with a single effort? Let's explore how this idiom captures that concept.[break 1s]The phrase is: 一举两得, yī jǔ liǎng dé.[break 0.5s]一 (yī) - one [break 0.5s]举 (jǔ) - to lift or to act [break 0.5s]两 (liǎng) - two [break 0.5s]得 (dé) - to gain or to obtain [break 1s]So, 一举两得 literally means 'one action, two gains.' Figuratively, it refers to achieving two benefits with a single action.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]The idiom originates from hunting practices in ancient China. A skilled hunter would aim at two birds with one arrow. If successful, he would not only provide food for himself but also ensure that he could share with his family, thus benefiting both himself and his loved ones. This clever strategy made the phrase popular as a metaphor for efficiency in achieving goals.[break 1.5s]Example one: 通过学习外语，他一举两得，不仅提升了自己的能力，还交到了很多朋友。[break 1s]By learning a foreign language, he achieved two gains: he not only improved his skills but also made many friends.[break 1s]Example two: 这项投资让公司一举两得，既增加了利润，又提升了品牌形象。[break 1s]This investment allowed the company to gain two benefits: it increased profits and enhanced the brand image.[break 1s]Example three: 参加这个活动，她一举两得，既锻炼了身体，又放松了心情。[break 1s]By participating in this event, she achieved two gains: she exercised her body and relaxed her mind.[break 1s]So, remember, 一举两得 means 'one action, two gains.' Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
